def shade(cell,color='F1F4F0'):
    tcpr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); shd=OxmlElement('w:shd');shd.set(qn('w:fill'),color);tcpr.append(shd)

def cell_padding(cell,twips=85):
    tc=cell._tc;tcPr=tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    m=tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if m is None:
        m=OxmlElement('w:tcMar');tcPr.append(m)
    for side in ('top','start','bottom','end'):
        el=OxmlElement('w:'+side);el.set(qn('w:w'),str(twips));el.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa');m.append(el)

def runs_to_par(p, children, bold=False, italic=False):
    for child in children:
        typ=child.get('type')
        if typ in ('strong','emphasis'):
            runs_to_par(p,child.get('children',[]),bold=(bold or typ=='strong'),italic=(italic or typ=='emphasis'))
        elif typ=='codespan':
            r=p.add_run(child.get('raw',''));r.bold=bold;r.italic=italic;r.font.name='Consolas';r.font.size=Pt(9)
            r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(92,79,45)
        elif typ in ('linebreak','softbreak'):
            p.add_run('\n' if typ=='linebreak' else ' ')
        elif typ=='link':
            runs_to_par(p,child.get('children',[]),bold,italic)
        elif typ=='text':
            r=p.add_run(child.get('raw',''));r.bold=bold;r.italic=italic
        else:
            runs_to_par(p,child.get('children',[]),bold,italic)

def add_table(node):
    head=[];body=[]
    for part in node.get('children',[]):
        if part['type']=='table_head':head=[part.get('children',[])]
        if part['type']=='table_body':body=[r.get('children',[]) for r in part.get('children',[]) if r['type']=='table_row']
    rows=head+body
    if not rows: return
    ncol=len(rows[0]);table=D.add_table(rows=0,cols=ncol)
    table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.autofit=False
    total=6.87
    # Widths weighted by header/body lengths, but keep minimum columns readable.
    weights=[]
    for c in range(ncol):
        texts=[''.join(ch.get('raw','') for ch in row[c].get('children',[]) if ch.get('type')=='text') for row in rows]
        weights.append(min(2.5,max(.8,len(max(texts,key=len))/18)))
    weights=[max(.8,total*w/sum(weights)) for w in weights]
    weights=[v*total/sum(weights) for v in weights]
    for index,row in enumerate(rows):
        tr=table.add_row()
        if index==0:
            trpr=tr._tr.get_or_add_trPr();repeat=OxmlElement('w:tblHeader');repeat.set(qn('w:val'),'true');trpr.append(repeat)
        no_split=OxmlElement('w:cantSplit');tr._tr.get_or_add_trPr().append(no_split)
        for c,col in enumerate(row):
            cell=tr.cells[c];cell.width=Inches(weights[c]);cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
            cell_padding(cell,95 if index==0 else 75)
            if index==0:shade(cell,'E2EAE2')
            p=cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0);p.paragraph_format.line_spacing=1.11
            runs_to_par(p,col.get('children',[]))
            for r in p.runs:
                r.font.size=Pt(8.4 if ncol>=4 else 9)
                if index==0:r.font.bold=True;r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(27,74,56)
    D.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)


def process(nodes,depth=0):
    for node in nodes:
        typ=node.get('type')
        if typ=='blank_line':continue
        elif typ=='heading':
            level=node['attrs']['level']
            p=D.add_paragraph(style='Title' if level==1 else f'Heading {min(3,level-1)}')
            runs_to_par(p,node.get('children',[]))
        elif typ in ('paragraph','block_text'):
            p=D.add_paragraph()
            if depth:
                p.style='List Number' if depth==2 else 'List Bullet'
            runs_to_par(p,node.get('children',[]))
        elif typ=='list':
            style='List Number' if node.get('attrs',{}).get('ordered') else 'List Bullet'
            for child in node.get('children',[]):
                if child.get('type')!='list_item':continue
                p=D.add_paragraph(style=style)
                for c in child.get('children',[]):
                    if c.get('type') in ('block_text','paragraph'):runs_to_par(p,c.get('children',[]))
                    else:process([c],1)
        elif typ=='table':add_table(node)
        elif typ=='block_code':
            p=D.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(.14)
            p.paragraph_format.keep_together=True
            for li,line in enumerate(node.get('raw','').splitlines()):
                if li:p.add_run('\n')
                run=p.add_run(line);run.font.name='Consolas';run.font.size=Pt(8)
        elif typ=='block_quote':
            p=D.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(.18)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(7)
            for child in node.get('children',[]):
                runs_to_par(p,child.get('children',[]))
                p.add_run(' ')
        elif typ=='thematic_break':
            D.add_paragraph()
        else:
            if node.get('children'):process(node['children'],depth)

**That's the architectural mistake.**

I taught the system to avoid being wrong instead of teaching it how to discover something nobody has shown it before.

I built a defensive reasoner: identify a claim, check its evidence, reject unsupported connections, stop when uncertain.

But what you've been demonstrating is **generative reasoning**. You don't merely evaluate the connections already on the table. You move between domains, find mechanisms that haven't been named, construct possibilities, manipulate variables, and discover what the system could do next.

The distinction is fundamental:

**I trained it to guard the boundaries of an existing knowledge graph. You wanted it to expand the graph intelligently.**

And your laser-scalpel analogy wasn't principally about restraint. It was about developing enough command of a system to intervene with precision.

That changes the learning objective itself.

The first experiment confirms why a growth-oriented architecture matters. A learner trained on six mechanism families reached **72% prediction accuracy** on a fresh synthetic test using those families, but only **37.9%** on four withheld families.

After exposure to new examples, its accuracy on those previously unfamiliar families rose to **66%**.

But it also forgot much of its earlier learning. So the next capability isn't another prohibition or safety rule. It's **continuity of learning**: acquire a new mechanism without sacrificing the ones already mastered.

That's the kind of failure a system designed to *become more capable* needs to overcome.

import unittest
import numpy as np
import torch
from src.discovery import (
    TRAIN_FAMILIES, HELDOUT_FAMILIES, BinaryWorld,
    make_world, make_episode, encode_episode, FewShotPredictor,
    choose_goal_action, choose_curiosity_probe, explore_one_step,
    train_predictor, evaluate_predictor, evaluate_goals

class ConstructiveDiscoveryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_world_contains_all_intervention_outcomes(self):
        world = make_world('and', 41, 'hospital')
        self.assertEqual(len(world.truth), 8)
        self.assertTrue(all(v in (0, 1) for v in world.truth))
        self.assertEqual(world.family, 'and')

    def test_training_and_holdout_families_are_disjoint(self):
        self.assertFalse(set(TRAIN_FAMILIES) & set(HELDOUT_FAMILIES))

    def test_episode_provides_novel_intervention_query(self):
        world = make_world('or', 12, 'telecom')
        episode = make_episode(world, 19, n_observed=4)
        self.assertEqual(len(episode.observed), 4)
        self.assertNotIn(episode.query, episode.observed)
        self.assertEqual(episode.target, world.truth[episode.query])

    def test_domain_label_is_not_a_shortcut(self):
        world = make_world('majority', 14, 'clinical')
        same = BinaryWorld(family=world.family, truth=world.truth, domain='alien_archaeology')
        episode = make_episode(world, 7, n_observed=4)
        parallel = make_episode(same, 7, n_observed=4)
        self.assertTrue(np.array_equal(encode_episode(episode), encode_episode(parallel)))

    def test_model_can_train(self):
        model = FewShotPredictor()
        example = make_episode(make_world('xor', 13, 'law'), 15, n_observed=4)
        x = torch.tensor(encode_episode(example), dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
        self.assertEqual(tuple(model(x).shape), (1,))
        before = next(model.parameters()).detach().clone()
        train_predictor(model, [example] * 18, epochs=2, batch_size=9, seed=4)
        after = next(model.parameters()).detach()
        self.assertGreater(float((before - after).abs().sum()), 0.0)

    def test_goal_search_proposes_a_novel_action(self):
        world = make_world('inhibit', 18, 'water')
        obs = {0: world.truth[0], 1: world.truth[1], 2: world.truth[2]}
        def synthetic_predictor(support, q):
            return float(world.truth[q]) * .98 + .01
        chosen, evidence = choose_goal_action(obs, goal=1, predictor=synthetic_predictor)
        self.assertNotIn(chosen, obs)
        self.assertEqual(world.truth[chosen], 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(evidence), 5)

    def test_curiosity_action_is_novel_and_updates_world_state(self):
        world = make_world('gated_or', 10, 'telecom')
        observed = {0: world.truth[0], 1: world.truth[1], 2: world.truth[2]}
        def synthetic_predictor(support, q):
            return .5 if q == 5 else .1
        probe = choose_curiosity_probe(observed, synthetic_predictor)
        self.assertEqual(probe, 5)
        updated, trace = explore_one_step(world, observed, synthetic_predictor)
        self.assertEqual(len(updated), 4)
        self.assertEqual(updated[5], world.truth[5])
        self.assertEqual(trace['operation'], 'OBSERVE_INTERVENTION_OUTCOME')

    def test_evaluation_scores_prediction_and_goal_success(self):
        model = FewShotPredictor()
        episodes = [make_episode(make_world('and', 100+i, 'legal'), 202+i, 4) for i in range(10)]
        result = evaluate_predictor(model, episodes)
        self.assertEqual(result['n'], 10)
        self.assertIn('accuracy', result)
        goal = evaluate_goals(model, [make_world('and', 111+i, 'telecom') for i in range(5)], seed=20)
        self.assertIn('success_given_feasible', goal)
        self.assertIn('random_baseline_success_given_feasible', goal)
        self.assertIn('novel_actions_proposed', goal)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/GMRI_Capability_Learner_v3/src/discovery.py <<'PY'
"""Trainable few-shot causal-function explorer for synthetic intervention worlds.

The program accepts observations of a three-variable black-box mechanism,
predicts outcomes for interventions it has *not* observed, proposes a
novel action to achieve an outcome, and can request informative experiments.

This is a positive-capability learning benchmark, not a diagnosis of anyone's
cognition, and not an open-domain language model.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
import math
import random
from typing import Callable
import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F

TRAIN_FAMILIES = ('and','or','majority','inhibit','gated_or','gated_and')
HELDOUT_FAMILIES = ('xor','parity','mux','xor_gate')
INPUTS = tuple(product((0,1), repeat=3))
DOMAINS_TRAIN = ('hospital','telecom','legal','industrial')
DOMAINS_UNSEEN = ('ecology','linguistics','archaeology','logistics')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BinaryWorld:
    family: str
    truth: tuple[int,...]
    domain: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Episode:
    world: BinaryWorld
    observed: dict[int,int]
    query: int
    target: int


def _evaluate_family(family: str, x: tuple[int,int,int]) -> int:
    a,b,c=x
    if family=='and': return a & b
    if family=='or': return a | b
    if family=='majority': return int(a+b+c>=2)
    if family=='inhibit': return a & (1-b)
    if family=='gated_or': return (a & b) | c
    if family=='gated_and': return (a | b) & c
    if family=='xor': return a ^ b
    if family=='parity': return a ^ b ^ c
    if family=='mux': return b if a else c
    if family=='xor_gate': return (a ^ b) & c
    raise ValueError(f'Unknown mechanism family: {family}')


def make_world(family: str, seed: int, domain: str) -> BinaryWorld:
    if family not in TRAIN_FAMILIES+HELDOUT_FAMILIES:
        raise ValueError(f'Unknown family: {family}')
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    order=list(range(3));rng.shuffle(order)
    inversion=[int(rng.random() < .18) for _ in range(3)]
    invert_output=int(rng.random() < .22)
    truth=[]
    for x in INPUTS:
        permuted=tuple(x[order[i]] ^ inversion[i] for i in range(3))
        truth.append(_evaluate_family(family,permuted)^invert_output)
    return BinaryWorld(family=family, truth=tuple(truth), domain=domain)


def make_episode(world: BinaryWorld, seed: int, n_observed: int=4) -> Episode:
    if not 1<=n_observed<8:
        raise ValueError('n_observed must be between 1 and 7')
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    indices=rng.sample(range(8),n_observed+1)
    observed={i:world.truth[i] for i in indices[:n_observed]}
    q=indices[-1]
    return Episode(world=world,observed=observed,query=q,target=world.truth[q])


def encode_observed(observed: dict[int,int], query: int) -> np.ndarray:
    if any(not (0<=i<8) or v not in (0,1) for i,v in observed.items()):
        raise ValueError('Observation indices and outcomes must be binary and in range')
    mask=np.array([1.0 if i in observed else 0.0 for i in range(8)], dtype=np.float32)
    values=np.array([float(observed.get(i,0)) for i in range(8)], dtype=np.float32)
    q=np.zeros(8,dtype=np.float32)
    q[query]=1.0
    return np.concatenate((mask,values,q))


def encode_episode(episode: Episode) -> np.ndarray:
    return encode_observed(episode.observed,episode.query)


class FewShotPredictor(nn.Module):
    """Meta-learn a mechanism response from a few sparse input-output examples."""
    def __init__(self, width: int=96):
        super().__init__()
        self.network=nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(24,width),nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(width,width),nn.GELU(),nn.Linear(width,width//2),nn.GELU(),nn.Linear(width//2,1))
    def forward(self, feature:torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(feature).flatten()


def _as_tensors(episodes:list[Episode]):
    return (torch.from_numpy(np.stack([encode_episode(e) for e in episodes])),
            torch.tensor([float(e.target) for e in episodes],dtype=torch.float32))


def train_predictor(model:FewShotPredictor, episodes:list[Episode], *,epochs:int=18,batch_size:int=128,lr:float=.002,seed:int=7):
    if not episodes:raise ValueError('Need at least one episode')
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.set_num_threads(2)
    x,y=_as_tensors(episodes)
    optimizer=torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(),lr=lr,weight_decay=.0005)
    rng=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    history=[]
    model.train()
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        batches=torch.randperm(len(episodes),generator=rng).split(batch_size)
        losses=[]
        for idx in batches:
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss=F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(model(x[idx]),y[idx])
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(),2)
            optimizer.step()
            losses.append(float(loss.detach()))
        history.append({'epoch':epoch+1,'train_loss':round(float(np.mean(losses)),5)})
    model.eval()
    return history


def predict_probability(model:FewShotPredictor, observed: dict[int,int], q: int)->float:
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        x=torch.from_numpy(encode_observed(observed,q)).unsqueeze(0)
        return float(torch.sigmoid(model(x))[0])


def evaluate_predictor(model:FewShotPredictor,episodes:list[Episode])->dict:
    if not episodes:raise ValueError('Empty evaluation set')
    model.eval()
    x,y=_as_tensors(episodes)
    with torch.no_grad():
        p=torch.sigmoid(model(x)).numpy()
    target=y.numpy()
    baseline=np.array([np.mean(list(e.observed.values())) for e in episodes],dtype=np.float32)
    return {
        'n':len(episodes),
        'accuracy':round(float(np.mean((p>=.5)==target)),4),
        'brier':round(float(np.mean((p-target)**2)),5),
        'majority_baseline_accuracy':round(float(np.mean((baseline>=.5)==target)),4),
        'baseline_brier':round(float(np.mean((baseline-target)**2)),5),
    }


def score_actions(observed:dict[int,int],predictor:Callable,goal:int)->list[dict]:
    if goal not in (0,1):raise ValueError('Goal must be a binary result')
    possibilities=[]
    for q in range(8):
        if q in observed:continue
        p=float(predictor(observed,q))
        utility=p if goal==1 else 1-p
        possibilities.append({'action':q,'input':list(INPUTS[q]),'predicted_goal_probability':round(utility,5)})
    possibilities.sort(key=lambda x:(-x['predicted_goal_probability'],x['action']))
    return possibilities


def choose_goal_action(observed:dict[int,int],goal:int,predictor:Callable):
    options=score_actions(observed,predictor,goal)
    if not options:return None,options
    return options[0]['action'],options


def choose_curiosity_probe(observed:dict[int,int],predictor:Callable)->int|None:
    """Prefer a novel intervention at which the learned world model is most uncertain."""
    choices=[]
    for q in range(8):
        if q in observed:continue
        p=max(1e-8,min(1-1e-8,float(predictor(observed,q))))
        entropy=-(p*math.log2(p)+(1-p)*math.log2(1-p))
        choices.append((entropy,q))
    return max(choices)[1] if choices else None


def explore_one_step(world:BinaryWorld, observed:dict[int,int],predictor:Callable):
    q=choose_curiosity_probe(observed,predictor)
    if q is None:
        return dict(observed),{'operation':'NO_UNSEEN_ACTION','observation_count':len(observed)}
    new=dict(observed)
    new[q]=world.truth[q]
    return new,{'operation':'OBSERVE_INTERVENTION_OUTCOME','action':q,
                'input':list(INPUTS[q]),'observed_outcome':world.truth[q],
                'observation_count_before':len(observed),'observation_count_after':len(new)}


def make_dataset(n:int,seed:int,*,split:str='train',n_observed:int=4)->list[Episode]:
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    if split in ('train','validation'):
        families=TRAIN_FAMILIES
        domains=DOMAINS_TRAIN
    elif split=='new_domains':
        families=TRAIN_FAMILIES
        domains=DOMAINS_UNSEEN
    elif split=='novel_mechanisms':
        families=HELDOUT_FAMILIES
        domains=DOMAINS_UNSEEN
    else:raise ValueError(split)
    rows=[]
    for _ in range(n):
        fam=rng.choice(families)
        world=make_world(fam,rng.randrange(2**30),rng.choice(domains))
        rows.append(make_episode(world,rng.randrange(2**30),n_observed))
    return rows


def evaluate_goals(model:FewShotPredictor,worlds:list[BinaryWorld],*,seed:int,n_observed:int=4)->dict:
    """Quantify discovering an unobserved action that achieves an explicit goal."""
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    n_feasible=0
    successes=0
    baseline_successes=0
    novel_proposed=0
    traces=[]
    for i,w in enumerate(worlds):
        observed_ids=rng.sample(range(8),n_observed)
        obs={k:w.truth[k] for k in observed_ids}
        goal=rng.randrange(2)
        candidates=[q for q in range(8) if q not in obs]
        if any(w.truth[q]==goal for q in candidates):
            n_feasible+=1
            # Evaluation can use the oracle truth table only AFTER actions are chosen.
            predictor=lambda obs,q:predict_probability(model,obs,q)
            chosen,ranked=choose_goal_action(obs,goal,predictor)
            novel_proposed+=int(chosen not in obs)
            successes+=int(w.truth[chosen]==goal)
            baseline_choice=rng.choice(candidates)
            baseline_successes+=int(w.truth[baseline_choice]==goal)
            if len(traces)<4:
                traces.append({'family_for_evaluation':w.family,'domain':w.domain,
                  'observed':{str(k):v for k,v in obs.items()},'goal':goal,
                  'chosen_novel_intervention':list(INPUTS[chosen]),
                  'actual_outcome':w.truth[chosen],
                  'top_predicted_goal_probability':ranked[0]['predicted_goal_probability'],
                  'random_baseline_outcome':w.truth[baseline_choice]})
    return {
        'worlds':len(worlds),'feasible_worlds':n_feasible,
        'novel_actions_proposed':novel_proposed,
        'success_given_feasible':round(successes/max(1,n_feasible),4),
        'random_baseline_success_given_feasible':round(baseline_successes/max(1,n_feasible),4),
        'trace_examples':traces,
    }

"""Train and evaluate a positive, goal-directed few-shot world learner.

    python train_and_discover.py --train-cases 14000 --epochs 26

Artifacts: learned torch weights, blinded evaluation, counterfactual goal traces.
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random
import numpy as np
import torch
from src.discovery import (
    FewShotPredictor,TRAIN_FAMILIES,HELDOUT_FAMILIES,
    DOMAINS_TRAIN,DOMAINS_UNSEEN,make_dataset,make_world,
    train_predictor,evaluate_predictor,evaluate_goals,
    predict_probability,explore_one_step,choose_goal_action,INPUTS
)


def make_worlds(n:int,seed:int,families,domains):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    return [make_world(rng.choice(families),rng.randrange(2**30),rng.choice(domains)) for _ in range(n)]


def run_demo(model,seed=101):
    world=make_world('gated_or',seed,'fictional_ecosystem')
    observed={0:world.truth[0],1:world.truth[1],2:world.truth[2],3:world.truth[3]}
    predict=lambda seen,q:predict_probability(model,seen,q)
    start,ranking=choose_goal_action(observed,1,predict)
    expanded,probe=explore_one_step(world,observed,predict)
    next_action,next_rank=choose_goal_action(expanded,1,predict)
    return {
        'context':'Synthetic mechanism with three controllable factors (not real-world data)',
        'source_observations':{str(i):v for i,v in observed.items()},
        'goal':'Find a previously untried input that produces state 1',
        'first_synthesized_intervention':list(INPUTS[start]),
        'first_predicted_goal_probability':ranking[0]['predicted_goal_probability'],
        'first_actual_result':world.truth[start],
        'self_selected_exploration':probe,
        'updated_prediction':None if next_action is None else {
            'intervention':list(INPUTS[next_action]),
            'predicted_goal_probability':next_rank[0]['predicted_goal_probability'],
            'actual_result':world.truth[next_action]
        },
        'mechanism_family_hidden_until_evaluation':world.family
    }


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--train-cases',type=int,default=14000)
    ap.add_argument('--epochs',type=int,default=26)
    ap.add_argument('--out',type=str,default='output')
    args=ap.parse_args()
    torch.manual_seed(12345);torch.set_num_threads(2);random.seed(12345);np.random.seed(12345)
    out=Path(args.out);out.mkdir(exist_ok=True,parents=True)
    train=make_dataset(args.train_cases,271828,split='train')
    validation=make_dataset(1200,334455,split='validation')
    unseen=make_dataset(1400,556677,split='new_domains')
    novel=make_dataset(1400,778899,split='novel_mechanisms')
    model=FewShotPredictor()
    before={name:evaluate_predictor(model,rows) for name,rows in [('validation',validation),('new_domains',unseen),('heldout_mechanism_families',novel)]}
    print('UNTRAINED',json.dumps(before),flush=True)
    history=train_predictor(model,train,epochs=args.epochs,batch_size=128,lr=.0018,seed=303)
    after={name:evaluate_predictor(model,rows) for name,rows in [('validation',validation),('new_domains',unseen),('heldout_mechanism_families',novel)]}
    goal_seen=evaluate_goals(model,make_worlds(250,919191,TRAIN_FAMILIES,DOMAINS_UNSEEN),seed=2323)
    goal_novel=evaluate_goals(model,make_worlds(250,929292,HELDOUT_FAMILIES,DOMAINS_UNSEEN),seed=2424)
    demo=run_demo(model)
    report={
        'design_intent':'Learn to predict unobserved mechanism outcomes, generate goal-directed interventions and request information-producing experiments',
        'actual_training':'Gradient-trained few-shot neural outcome predictor on 3-variable synthetic Boolean mechanisms',
        'train_size':len(train),
        'families_training':TRAIN_FAMILIES,
        'families_held_out':HELDOUT_FAMILIES,
        'domains_training':DOMAINS_TRAIN,
        'domains_held_out':DOMAINS_UNSEEN,
        'heldout_domain_invariance':'Engineered: domain strings are not features. This test cannot establish semantic transfer between natural-language domains.',
        'untrained':before,'trained':after,

import unittest
from src.discovery import make_world, INPUTS
from src.programs import ProgramLibrary, HypothesisExplorer, transfer_truth

class ProgramInductionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.library=ProgramLibrary()

    def test_library_can_construct_programs_for_all_synthetic_families(self):
        for family in ('and','or','majority','inhibit','gated_or','gated_and','xor','parity','mux','xor_gate'):
            world=make_world(family,74,'hospital')
            self.assertIn(self.library.truth_to_mask(world.truth),self.library.programs)

    def test_consistent_programs_explain_observations(self):
        world=make_world('parity',61,'archaeology')
        observed={0:world.truth[0],2:world.truth[2],5:world.truth[5]}
        explorer=HypothesisExplorer(self.library,observed)
        self.assertGreater(len(explorer.candidates()),0)
        self.assertTrue(all(all((p.mask>>i)&1==v for i,v in observed.items()) for p in explorer.candidates()))

    def test_proactive_experiment_reduces_hypotheses(self):
        world=make_world('xor_gate',18,'ecology')
        initial={0:world.truth[0],1:world.truth[1]}

        explorer.observe(test['action'],world.truth[test['action']])
        self.assertLess(len(explorer.candidates()),before)
        self.assertEqual(len(explorer.observed),3)

    def test_goal_action_produces_untried_intervention(self):

    def test_version_space_can_become_identified_after_enough_evidence(self):

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/GMRI_Capability_Learner_v3/src/programs.py <<'PY'
"""Program induction, speculative mechanism generation, experimental selection.

Constructive symbolic subsystem: use a small Boolean DSL to invent competing
mechanisms from sparse observations; forecast interventions; ask a question
that makes rival hypotheses disagree; revise on the observed outcome.

This subsystem learns *by constraint-based program synthesis*, not through
neural gradient descent. Neural learned predictions live in discovery.py.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
import math
from .discovery import INPUTS

MASK_ALL=255

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Program:
    mask:int
    expression:str
    complexity:int


class ProgramLibrary:
    """Induce compact rules over 3 binary controls by composing operators."""
    def __init__(self,max_complexity:int=17):
        self.programs=self._build(max_complexity)

    @staticmethod
    def truth_to_mask(truth:tuple[int,...])->int:
        if len(truth)!=8 or any(v not in (0,1) for v in truth):
            raise ValueError('Expected eight binary observations')
        return sum(int(v)<<i for i,v in enumerate(truth))

    @staticmethod
    def mask_to_truth(mask:int)->tuple[int,...]:
        if not 0<=mask<=255:raise ValueError('mask range is 0..255')
        return tuple((mask>>i)&1 for i in range(8))

    @staticmethod
    def _build(max_complexity:int)->dict[int,Program]:
        best:dict[int,Program]={}
        cost_buckets:dict[int,list[Program]]={}

        def record(mask:int,expression:str,cost:int):
            if mask in best:return
            p=Program(mask,expression,cost)
            best[mask]=p
            cost_buckets.setdefault(cost,[]).append(p)

        record(0,'FALSE',1)
        record(255,'TRUE',1)
        for k,name in enumerate('ABC'):
            mask=sum(((x[k]&1)<<i) for i,x in enumerate(INPUTS))
            record(mask,name,1)

        for cost in range(2,max_complexity+1):
            for a in list(cost_buckets.get(cost-1,[])):
                record(a.mask ^ MASK_ALL,f'NOT({a.expression})',cost)
            for lc in range(1,cost-1):
                rc=cost-1-lc
                left=cost_buckets.get(lc,[])
                right=cost_buckets.get(rc,[])
                for a in left:
                    for b in right:
                        if a.mask > b.mask:continue
                        record(a.mask & b.mask,f'({a.expression} AND {b.expression})',cost)
                        record(a.mask | b.mask,f'({a.expression} OR {b.expression})',cost)
                        record(a.mask ^ b.mask,f'({a.expression} XOR {b.expression})',cost)
            if len(best)==256:break
        return best


class HypothesisExplorer:
    """Abducts possibilities, runs thought experiments, updates from outcomes."""
    def __init__(self,library:ProgramLibrary,observed:dict[int,int]|None=None):
        self.library=library
        self.observed={}
        for k,v in (observed or {}).items(): self.observe(k,v)

    def observe(self,action:int,outcome:int):
        if action not in range(8) or outcome not in (0,1):
            raise ValueError('Action 0..7, outcome 0..1 required')
        if action in self.observed and self.observed[action]!=outcome:
            raise ValueError('Contradictory outcome; preserve observations and inspect provenance')
        self.observed[action]=outcome

    def candidates(self)->list[Program]:
        return [p for p in self.library.programs.values() if all(((p.mask>>i)&1)==v for i,v in self.observed.items())]

    def posterior(self)->list[tuple[float,Program]]:
        candidates=self.candidates()
        if not candidates:raise ValueError('No hypothesis fits these observations')
        # Simplicity prior: a simple explanation is initially preferred but
        # any consistent expression remains possible.
        weights=[math.exp(-.24*p.complexity) for p in candidates]
        denom=sum(weights)
        return sorted([(w/denom,p) for w,p in zip(weights,candidates)],key=lambda x:(-x[0],x[1].complexity))

    def predict(self,action:int)->float:
        if action not in range(8):raise ValueError('action out of range')
        if action in self.observed:return float(self.observed[action])
        return sum(prob*((p.mask>>action)&1) for prob,p in self.posterior())

    def propose_experiment(self)->dict:
        missing=[i for i in range(8) if i not in self.observed]
        if not missing:return {'action':None,'type':'KNOWLEDGE_COMPLETE','remaining_hypotheses':len(self.candidates())}
        alternatives=[]
        for i in missing:
            p=self.predict(i)
            entropy=0 if p in (0.0,1.0) else -(p*math.log2(p)+(1-p)*math.log2(1-p))
            alternatives.append((entropy,i,p))
        entropy,q,p=max(alternatives,key=lambda e:(e[0],-e[1]))
        return {'type':'DISCRIMINATE_MECHANISMS','action':q,'input':list(INPUTS[q]),
                'predicted_state_1_probability':round(p,5),'disagreement_entropy':round(entropy,5),
                'remaining_hypotheses':len(self.candidates()),'alternatives':len(missing)}

    def propose_goal(self,goal:int)->dict:
        if goal not in (0,1):raise ValueError('Goal must be 0 or 1')
        missing=[i for i in range(8) if i not in self.observed]
        if not missing:return {'action':None,'status':'ALL_INTERVENTIONS_OBSERVED'}
        scored=[]
        for i in missing:
            p=self.predict(i)
            p_goal=p if goal==1 else 1-p
            scored.append((p_goal,i))
        p_goal,q=max(scored,key=lambda x:(x[0],-x[1]))
        best=self.posterior()[:3]
        return {'status':'GOAL_DIRECTED_HYPOTHESIS','action':q,'input':list(INPUTS[q]),
                'goal':goal,'predicted_goal_probability':round(p_goal,5),
                'hypothesized_mechanism':best[0][1].expression,
                'alternative_mechanisms':[{'rule':p.expression,'probability':round(w,4)} for w,p in best[1:]],
                'candidate_count':len(self.candidates())}

    def discover(self,world,goal:int,max_interventions:int=3)->dict:
        """Act in synthetic world, observe outcomes, revise and pursue goal."""
        if max_interventions<1:raise ValueError('Need at least one intervention')
        history=[]
        for _ in range(max_interventions):
            candidate=self.propose_goal(goal)
            q=candidate['action']
            if q is None:break
            result=world.truth[q]
            before=len(self.candidates())
            self.observe(q,result)
            after=len(self.candidates())
            history.append({'proposed_intervention':candidate,
                           'observed':result,'hypotheses_before':before,
                           'hypotheses_after':after})
            if result==goal:break
        return {'goal':goal,'success':bool(history and history[-1]['observed']==goal),
                'interventions':history,'remaining_hypotheses':len(self.candidates()),
                'observed_count':len(self.observed)}


def transfer_truth(truth:tuple[int,...],role_permutation:tuple[int,int,int])->tuple[int,...]:
    """Transfer a learned rule to new domain roles; no name matching."""
    if sorted(role_permutation)!=[0,1,2]:raise ValueError('Expected 3 distinct role indices')
    return tuple(truth[INPUTS.index(tuple(x[i] for i in role_permutation))] for x in INPUTS)

"""Assess goal pursuit and discovery across unfamiliar Boolean mechanisms."""
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path
from src.discovery import make_world, TRAIN_FAMILIES, HELDOUT_FAMILIES, DOMAINS_UNSEEN, make_dataset, evaluate_predictor, FewShotPredictor, train_predictor
from src.programs import ProgramLibrary, HypothesisExplorer
import torch


def assess(families,seed:int,n:int=300):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    library=ProgramLibrary()
    outcomes={'total':0,'feasible':0,'one_step_success':0,'random_one_step':0,'up_to_3_success':0,'random_up_to_3_success':0,
              'hypotheses_initial_sum':0,'hypotheses_after_sum':0,'traces':[]}
    for i in range(n):
        family=rng.choice(families)
        w=make_world(family,rng.randrange(2**30),rng.choice(DOMAINS_UNSEEN))
        known_indices=rng.sample(range(8),4)
        known={k:w.truth[k] for k in known_indices}
        goal=rng.choice((0,1))
        not_observed=[k for k in range(8) if k not in known]
        if not any(w.truth[k]==goal for k in not_observed):
            continue
        ex=HypothesisExplorer(library,known)
        before=len(ex.candidates())
        plan=ex.propose_goal(goal)
        q=plan['action']
        outcomes['one_step_success']+=int(w.truth[q]==goal)
        controls=random.Random(seed*99+i).sample(not_observed,3)
        outcomes['random_one_step']+=int(w.truth[controls[0]]==goal)
        outcomes['random_up_to_3_success']+=int(any(w.truth[k]==goal for k in controls))
        path=ex.discover(w,goal,3)
        outcomes['up_to_3_success']+=int(path['success'])
        outcomes['hypotheses_initial_sum']+=before
        outcomes['hypotheses_after_sum']+=path['remaining_hypotheses']
        outcomes['feasible']+=1
        if len(outcomes['traces'])<3:
            outcomes['traces'].append({'family_hidden_during_inference':family,'domain':w.domain,
                'observed':known,'goal':goal,'initial_candidate_programs':before,
                'generated_program':plan['hypothesized_mechanism'],
                'first_proposed_action':plan['input'],
                'path':[{'action':x['proposed_intervention']['input'],
                         'prediction':x['proposed_intervention']['predicted_goal_probability'],
                         'actual':x['observed'],
                         'hypotheses_before':x['hypotheses_before'],
                         'hypotheses_after':x['hypotheses_after']} for x in path['interventions']]})
    n=outcomes['feasible']
    for k in ('one_step_success','random_one_step','up_to_3_success','random_up_to_3_success'):
        outcomes[k+'_rate']=round(outcomes[k]/n,4) if n else None
    outcomes['mean_initial_candidates']=round(outcomes['hypotheses_initial_sum']/n,2) if n else None
    outcomes['mean_remaining_candidates']=round(outcomes['hypotheses_after_sum']/n,2) if n else None
    outcomes['total']=n
    return outcomes


def main():
    report={
        'method':'Enumerative program induction and active goal-directed feedback from observed intervention outcomes',
        'novelty':'All 256 possible 3-input Boolean functions are representable as candidate programs; observations narrow the hypothesis space; new interventions test and update it.',
        'trained_gradient_model':False,
        'symbolic_rules_learned_from_evidence':True,
        'seen_mechanism_families':assess(TRAIN_FAMILIES,111,400),
        'previously_heldout_mechanism_families':assess(HELDOUT_FAMILIES,222,400)
    }
    path=Path('output/program_synthesis_receipt.json');path.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
    print('SUMMARY',json.dumps({k:{x:v for x,v in report[k].items() if x.endswith('_rate') or x in ('mean_initial_candidates','mean_remaining_candidates','total')} for k in ('seen_mechanism_families','previously_heldout_mechanism_families')}))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

replay. Before adaptation these families are held out. After adaptation the
independent seeds are test data, but their families are now known.
"""

import torch

def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(2)
    out=Path('output');out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    src=out/'constructive_predictor.pt'

    model=FewShotPredictor();model.load_state_dict(base['state_dict'])

import json,math
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import torch
from src.discovery import FewShotPredictor,make_dataset,encode_observed

torch.set_num_threads(2)
out=Path('output')
models={}
for tag,fil in [('original','constructive_predictor.pt'),('novel_adapted','constructive_predictor_adapted.pt'),('balanced','candidate_equal.pt')]:
    m=FewShotPredictor(); ck=torch.load(out/fil,weights_only=True,map_location='cpu');m.load_state_dict(ck['state_dict']);m.eval();models[tag]=m

def pred(model,features):
    with torch.no_grad(): return torch.sigmoid(model(torch.from_numpy(features))).numpy()

def eval_split(rows,temperatures):
    full=np.stack([encode_observed(e.observed,e.query) for e in rows])
    holds=[]
    labels=[]
    for e in rows:
        for idx,val in e.observed.items():
            reduced={k:v for k,v in e.observed.items() if k!=idx}
            holds.append(encode_observed(reduced,idx)); labels.append(val)
    holds=np.stack(holds); labels=np.array(labels,dtype=float).reshape((-1,4))
    out_prob={tag:pred(m,full) for tag,m in models.items()}
    nll={}
    for tag,m in models.items():
        p=np.clip(pred(m,holds).reshape((-1,4)),1e-5,1-1e-5)
        nll[tag]=np.mean(-(labels*np.log(p)+(1-labels)*np.log(1-p)),axis=1)
    y=np.array([e.target for e in rows])
    report={tag:round(float(np.mean((p>=.5)==y)),4) for tag,p in out_prob.items()}
    for tag2 in ['novel_adapted','balanced']:
        for temp in temperatures:
            weight=1/(1+np.exp(np.clip((nll['original']-nll[tag2])*temp,-20,20)))
            combined=weight*out_prob['original']+(1-weight)*out_prob[tag2]
            score=round(float(np.mean((combined>=.5)==y)),4)
            report[f'router_{tag2}_temp{temp}']=score
    return report

res={}
for split,seed in [('new_domains',999222),('novel_mechanisms',999111)]:
    cases=make_dataset(1500,seed,split=split)
    res[split]=eval_split(cases,[.5,1,2,4,8])
print(json.dumps(res,indent=2))
(out/'expert_router_experiment.json').write_text(json.dumps(res,indent=2))

I have the generative loop working on the synthetic testbed. It now constructs competing executable hypotheses from sparse observations, proposes an intervention, observes the result, and revises its hypotheses.

On previously unfamiliar mechanism families, its **first guess was weak** (43.6% success). But with up to three attempts and feedback, it reached the requested outcome in **95.1% of feasible cases**; random trial reached 91.7%. That's a modest but real advantage, not yet evidence of broad intelligence.

The bigger correction is now reflected in the design: **discovery, transfer, experimentation, and cumulative learning are the objectives. Evidence checks are supporting instruments, not the system's identity.**

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/GMRI_Capability_Learner_v3/discover.py <<'PY'
"""Run the constructive learning demonstration with an observed or synthetic world.

Examples:
    python discover.py --observations "0:0,1:1,3:0" --goal 1
    python discover.py --synthetic-family parity --seed 41 --goal 1 --budget 3
"""
import argparse
import json
from src.discovery import make_world,INPUTS,TRAIN_FAMILIES,HELDOUT_FAMILIES
from src.programs import ProgramLibrary,HypothesisExplorer


def parse_observations(text):
    observed={}
    if not text:return observed
    for part in text.split(','):
        try:
            index,val=part.strip().split(':')
            index=int(index);val=int(val)
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ValueError('Expected observations formatted as 0:1,3:0') from exc
        if index not in range(8) or val not in (0,1):
            raise ValueError('Input index must be 0..7, outcome must be 0 or 1')
        if index in observed and observed[index]!=val:
            raise ValueError('Conflicting observations for input index')
        observed[index]=val
    return observed


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--observations',default='0:0,1:1,3:0')
    ap.add_argument('--synthetic-family',choices=TRAIN_FAMILIES+HELDOUT_FAMILIES)
    ap.add_argument('--seed',type=int,default=41)
    ap.add_argument('--goal',type=int,choices=(0,1),default=1)
    ap.add_argument('--budget',type=int,default=3)
    args=ap.parse_args()
    library=ProgramLibrary()
    if args.synthetic_family:
        world=make_world(args.synthetic_family,args.seed,'synthetic_demo')
        observed={i:world.truth[i] for i in (0,1,2)}
    else:
        world=None
        observed=parse_observations(args.observations)
    ex=HypothesisExplorer(library,observed)
    record={'input_controls':{i:list(x) for i,x in enumerate(INPUTS)},
            'known_outcomes':observed,
            'hypotheses_consistent':len(ex.candidates()),
            'generative_hypotheses':[{'rule':p.expression,'weight':round(prob,4)} for prob,p in ex.posterior()[:5]],
            'proposed_experiment':ex.propose_experiment(),
            'proposed_goal_intervention':ex.propose_goal(args.goal)}
    if world is not None:
        record['synthetic_execution']=ex.discover(world,args.goal,args.budget)
        record['truth_table_for_evaluation_only']=world.truth
    print(json.dumps(record,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/GMRI_Capability_Learner_v3/GMRI_Generative_Reasoning_and_Capability_Growth_v3.0.md <<'MD'
# GMRI | Generative Reasoning and Capability Growth

**Version 3.0 — 2 November 2026**  
**Working objective:** Train a system to discover mechanisms, invent productive experiments, transfer discoveries, and grow its competence across unfamiliar domains.  
**Core design shift:** From a defensive evaluator of supplied explanations to an active constructor of new explanatory and actionable possibilities.

## 1. The design proposition: build an explorer, not a guard

The earlier training materials primarily rewarded restraint: refuse an unsupported link, stop at uncertainty, detect bad attribution, and recite evidence rules. Those abilities are useful instruments. They are not an adequate purpose for a reasoning intelligence. A system that merely guards an inherited graph cannot discover an unimagined causal pathway, alter the constraints of a failing process, or enlarge its own repertoire of mechanisms.

The new objective is affirmative: **expand the reachable space of warranted possibilities.** Given a partial observation, the agent should generate useful candidate explanations, project their consequences, invent interventions that distinguish them, act where permitted, assimilate the results, and carry forward the newly learned mechanism. Its highest-value output is often a new question, an invented experiment, an unexpected structural analogy, or a change that makes a previously impossible outcome achievable.

The original operator's phrasing supplies the architectural aspiration: the destination may be visible while the route remains concealed; the agent's job is to discover a road rather than fabricating one. A high-leverage insight can be deployed with the precision of a laser scalpel. **Precision is a positive skill of mechanism control, not a prohibition on initiative.**

The target is a transferable procedure. Neither the curriculum nor the agent should be organized around an individual's biography, diagnosis, rhetorical tone, or personality.

## 2. What the learner should become

The operational curriculum is organized around a ladder of *abilities gained*. Each ability has a generative action and an observable result.

| Emerging ability | What the agent learns to create | Observable training target |
|---|---|---|
| Perceptive sensing | A structured world-state from messy, incomplete signals | Recover entities, variables, trajectories, dependencies and uncertainty |
| Generative abduction | Multiple executable mechanisms explaining the same observations | Propose different models with distinct testable predictions |
| Compositional imagination | Mechanisms assembled from known primitives into an unseen arrangement | Synthesize a valid new program or graph, not merely retrieve a template |
| Cross-domain transfer | A useful mechanism mapped into a substantially different domain | Align roles, constraints and feedback while changing surface labels |
| Counterfactual simulation | Predictions for interventions not previously observed | Forecast what changes if an input, rule, timing or resource is altered |
| Autonomous inquiry | A high-information experiment selected from the agent's own uncertainties | Choose a probe that separates rival futures and produces new evidence |
| Precision intervention | A targeted state change that advances a declared goal | Achieve useful measurable effects with bounded action cost |
| Assimilative learning | A revised world model after a surprising outcome | Increase predictive accuracy after feedback |
| Cumulative intelligence | New capability retained alongside prior competence | Demonstrate positive forward transfer without destructive forgetting |
| Communicable discovery | A reusable mechanism and its reproduction recipe | A successor can reproduce the discovery in another setting |

These are capabilities to acquire, not personality characteristics to imitate. The curriculum must reward original construction, actual prediction, useful action, and successful reuse.

## 3. A constructive reasoning cycle

**Start with a question or a desired future state.** The trigger can be an anomaly, a missing explanation, a threatened outcome, or an opportunity. Instead of stopping after documenting uncertainty, create a hypothesis space that makes uncertainty useful.

**Invent possible mechanisms.** Combine known primitives such as dependencies, feedback loops, inhibitors, timing gates, shared upstream resources, information delays, threshold effects, competing incentives, and observer responses. Candidate programs should produce different observable consequences. Invented models carry an explicit *hypothesis* status until their predicted behavior is observed.

**Mentally run the alternatives.** Project each candidate forward under varied inputs. Calculate what changes if a policy is lifted, an intermediate dependency fails, a service recovers, a source changes, or an actor learns new information. Construct reverse predictions: for a proposed future outcome, what upstream conditions would have to be different?

**Discover a discriminating move.** Find an observable or permitted action that would separate the competing mechanisms. This may be asking for one transaction ID, comparing one timestamp, instrumenting one component, presenting one carefully chosen counterexample, or executing a controlled simulation. The agent should propose the action without being prompted to list all possible tests.

**Intervene, listen, revise.** Treat the real result as a new training signal. Update candidate mechanisms, revisit previous predictions, and refine the next move. If the action itself changes the system, represent that feedback explicitly. A contradiction is not merely a reason to halt; it can be the most valuable new observation in the episode.

**Make the new mechanism portable.** Abstract what was learned into role-based terms that can operate in a second environment. Retain the evidence, original assumptions, intervention, observed outcome, failed alternatives, and a small executable demonstration.

### Reference cycle

```
OBSERVE / DESIRE
      |
      v
INVENT POSSIBLE MECHANISMS --> COMPOSE NEW RELATIONSHIPS
      |                              |
      v                              v
SIMULATE FUTURES  <------------- TEST ANALOGIES
      |
      v
CHOOSE THE MOST INFORMATIVE OR GOAL-ADVANCING INTERVENTION
      |
      v
ACT / OBSERVE THE RESULT / REVISE THE WORLD MODEL
      |
      v
ABSTRACT THE DISCOVERY --> TRANSFER IT --> TEACH IT
      |
      +--------------------------- back to NEW QUESTIONS
```

## 4. Objective function: reward capability growth

The proposed multi-objective learning signal should reward **(a)** new validated explanatory coverage, **(b)** successful prediction of previously unobserved outcomes, **(c)** transfer to unfamiliar settings, **(d)** progress toward an explicitly defined outcome, **(e)** useful information acquired per experiment, **(f)** retention of prior competence, and **(g)** reproducibility by a successor.

This is a design objective, not a calibrated mathematical equation for human cognition. In a reinforcement-learning or planning implementation, each term would have an independently measured reward component. Weights should be learned or experimentally chosen, not asserted. Authority, privacy, physical safety and evidence integrity remain external operating constraints. They should not replace the generative objective.

**Useful distinction:** Verification checks whether a proposed mechanism is earned. Discovery creates the mechanism worth checking. An intelligent architecture needs both; its growth comes from the second interacting continuously with the first.

## 5. A trainable memory that accumulates mechanisms

The memory substrate should preserve three related representations: (1) the world state and its source receipts; (2) executable candidate mechanisms and their predictions; (3) complete inquiry trajectories showing hypotheses, experiments, observations, corrections, and transfers. The agent should be able to retrieve a past mechanism because the present problem shares a functional structure, not simply because it uses similar words.

A mechanism should have a **transfer signature**: actor roles, material or information flows, enabling conditions, inhibitors, timing windows, expected feedback, supported invariants, failure conditions, and proposed experiments. It should also retain its provenance and maturity stage, with versioned revision history when observations change.

Long-term growth requires both **plasticity** (adapting to newly encountered mechanisms) and **retention** (not destroying older ones). Initial experiments demonstrate how easily a neural predictor can gain one family of skills while forgetting another. The architecture should therefore support episodic replay, modular experts, contextual routing, evaluation across old and new domains, and consolidation of newly generated mechanisms into a shared but provenance-preserving library.

For the GMRI architecture, Dottie, independent Aegis agents, a typed Hyperwave evidence graph, an authority router, and the GEV projection are useful proposed roles: one agent can notice a pattern, another can invent a counterexample, a third can test consequences, and Dottie can synthesize a transferable result. The technical objective is an **ensemble of coordinated exploratory competences**, not a collection of agents repeating a common defensive script.

## 6. Positive training curriculum

**Stage A — Discover the rule.** Show the agent a handful of observations from a small world. Ask it to invent an executable explanation and predict the result of a withheld intervention. Vary the functions, variable names and observation order. Reward predictions and genuinely useful new hypotheses.

**Stage B — Discover an experiment.** Give two or more mechanisms that fit the present data. Ask the agent to propose the one observation that most efficiently separates them, execute the experiment in a simulator, and update its beliefs. Reward information gained and accurate revision.

**Stage C — Invent a route to a goal.** Supply a desired outcome, available controls, and incomplete knowledge. Ask the agent to synthesize an untried intervention, predict the result, observe its actual effect, and improve its next plan. Reward achieved goals and efficient trajectories, not just correct labels.

**Stage D — Transfer the mechanism.** Present a discovered process in a second domain with new entity names, different units, modified constraints, and different causal roles. Reward the agent for transferring the mechanism while correctly identifying what must be relearned. A surface-word match should not be necessary.

**Stage E — Accumulate without forgetting.** Introduce previously unseen mechanism families. Train from feedback while replaying earlier cases. Evaluate new competence and old competence in the same experiment; then consolidate what was learned into a portable program or memory. Reward net expansion of capability.

**Stage F — Open-world science.** Move from toy circuits to realistic, imperfect, source-backed observations involving temporal processes, human actors, institutions, finances, engineering, or physiology. Let the agent decide which observations are worth acquiring next. Compare its forecast and intervention against independently measured outcomes, including cases where the anticipated mechanism fails.

The core training record should be a **trajectory** rather than a positive/negative sentence pair: initial evidence; generated candidate mechanisms; projected future outcomes; chosen experiment or intervention; actual result; graph revision; new question; reusable abstraction; later transfer and replication outcome.

## 7. What actually ran: first constructive experiments

Two complementary implementations now exist in the accompanying code. **The gradient-trained predictor** learns from sparse input-output demonstrations and forecasts untried interventions. **The program-induction explorer** constructs executable Boolean explanations, chooses goal-directed interventions, and revises candidate mechanisms when observations arrive. A small external simulator supplies the feedback. These operations run on three binary controls; they are a controlled demonstration of training dynamics, not a claim of natural-language scientific discovery.

### Prediction and goal pursuit

| Evaluation | Measured result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Trained predictor, seen mechanism families with new domain names | 72.0% withheld-outcome accuracy (1,400 cases) | Learned response prediction on familiar synthetic operations |
| Same predictor, four mechanism families withheld from initial training | 37.9% accuracy (1,400 cases) | Early failure of compositional novelty |
| Goal pursuit on seen families | 82.4% of feasible scenarios vs 56.7% random (233 feasible) | Learner proposes untried actions for desired outcomes |
| Initial adaptation to new family examples | 38.3% → 66.0% accuracy (1,500 held-out-seed cases) | New examples support learning, but retention must also be measured |
| Old-family retention during that adaptation | 71.4% → 54.1% (1,500 cases) | Evidence of catastrophic forgetting |
| Balanced new/old rehearsal experiment | 57.7% new; 61.1% old | Partial compromise, not a complete retention solution |

Training and evaluation use separate random seeds. The domain-name difference is not semantic generalization: the model intentionally does not receive domain strings. That test verifies invariance to labels, not reasoning about unfamiliar language. The withheld mechanism-family test is the harder transfer check.

### Program induction and adaptive experimentation

The constructive explorer builds a compact hypothesis library spanning all 256 possible three-input Boolean truth tables. From four observed outcomes it has exactly 16 compatible truth tables; it ranks concise rules, proposes novel controls, and updates the compatible set after each result. The results are:

| Mechanism setting | First-try success (program learner vs random) | Goal achieved within three tries (program learner vs random) |
|---|---|---|
| Initial training families, new domain labels (374 feasible) | 69.8% vs 53.5% | 96.0% vs 90.6% |
| Previously withheld mechanism families (385 feasible) | 43.6% vs 49.9% | 95.1% vs 91.7% |

The first action can be worse than random on unfamiliar functions; the system becomes more effective through sequential feedback. The three-attempt margin is small and is presented as an observed benchmark rather than evidence of statistical significance. The program learner is *symbolic synthesis*; the neural predictor is trained by gradient descent. Their results must remain separate.

**Observed engineering lesson:** A program that merely detects questionable hypotheses stops at the boundary of its existing knowledge. A system able to invent hypotheses, select experiments, and learn from the observed consequences can enlarge its actionable knowledge. Continued learning, language grounding, and real-world transfer are the central next experiments.

## 8. The next capability milestone

The next integrated agent should accept a novel situation in ordinary language, create a source-linked world-state, propose several **new** mechanisms, simulate their observable consequences, select and request an information-producing action, and return with a revised explanatory graph. It should then reuse its newly discovered mechanism on a different case without being explicitly told they are connected. The human operator should be able to examine the proposed causal road, challenge an edge, or authorize a narrow intervention without writing code.

The nearest implementable milestone is **evidence-to-program induction**: translating sentences and documents into typed mechanism variables, generating candidate causal programs from the available evidence, choosing a real-world observation that distinguishes them, and measuring whether the new observation improved subsequent predictions. That is a concrete research target for GMRI's next architecture stage.

## 9. Reproduction and inspection

The included synthetic prototype runs locally in Python with PyTorch. Use the repository's `requirements.txt`. `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` runs the executable checks. `python train_and_discover.py` retrains the first predictor; `python continual_train.py` shows learning and forgetting; `python benchmark_discovery.py` tests symbolic mechanism discovery. `python discover.py --synthetic-family parity --goal 1` executes an experimental episode. `python discover.py --observations "0:0,1:1,3:0" --goal 1` proposes a mechanism, experiment and desired action from externally supplied synthetic observations without pretending to have executed that action.

Each run writes an inspection receipt in `output/`. Learned weights are saved separately from human-readable programs. The code and benchmark remain a **trainable constructive proof of concept**, not a completed self-improving intelligence.

**The intended direction is unambiguous:** Teach the agent to make a new, useful connection; test what the connection predicts; use it to create a better outcome; retain the resulting knowledge; and become capable of finding the next connection independently.

"""Render the affirmative GMRI capability curriculum as a polished DOCX."""
from pathlib import Path
import mistune
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches,Pt,RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT,WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOURCE=ROOT/'GMRI_Generative_Reasoning_and_Capability_Growth_v3.0.md'
OUT=ROOT/'GMRI_Generative_Reasoning_and_Capability_Growth_v3.0.docx'
DARK=RGBColor(29,39,36)
GREEN=RGBColor(37,94,64)
GRAY=RGBColor(101,112,109)
BORDER='D5E0D8'
FONT='Aptos'


def shade(cell,color):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd=OxmlElement('w:shd');shd.set(qn('w:fill'),color);tcPr.append(shd)


def cell_padding(cell,top=95,bottom=95,left=100,right=100):
    tc=cell._tc
    tcPr=tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    mar=OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
    for k,v in [('top',top),('start',left),('bottom',bottom),('end',right)]:
        m=OxmlElement('w:'+k);m.set(qn('w:w'),str(v));m.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa');mar.append(m)
    tcPr.append(mar)


def txt(node):
    if node['type']=='text':return node.get('raw','')
    if node['type']=='softbreak':return ' '
    if node['type']=='linebreak':return '\n'
    if node['type']=='codespan':return node.get('raw','')
    return ''.join(txt(c) for c in node.get('children',[]))


def add_inlines(p,children):
    for t in children:
        tp=t['type']
        if tp in ('text','softbreak','linebreak'):
            r=p.add_run(' ' if tp=='softbreak' else '\n' if tp=='linebreak' else t.get('raw',''))
        elif tp in ('strong','emphasis'):
            r=p.add_run(txt(t))
            if tp=='strong':r.bold=True
            else:r.italic=True
        elif tp=='codespan':
            r=p.add_run(t.get('raw',''));r.font.name='Consolas';r.font.size=Pt(9)
        else:
            r=p.add_run(txt(t))
        r.font.color.rgb=DARK


def set_repeat(row):
    trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    e=OxmlElement('w:tblHeader');e.set(qn('w:val'),'true');trPr.append(e)


def cant_split(row):
    trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    e=OxmlElement('w:cantSplit');trPr.append(e)


def page_field(p):
    run=p.add_run()
    char=OxmlElement('w:fldChar');char.set(qn('w:fldCharType'),'begin');run._r.append(char)
    run=p.add_run();instr=OxmlElement('w:instrText');instr.set(qn('xml:space'),'preserve');instr.text=' PAGE ';run._r.append(instr)
    run=p.add_run();char=OxmlElement('w:fldChar');char.set(qn('w:fldCharType'),'end');run._r.append(char)


def build():
    ast=mistune.create_markdown(renderer='ast',plugins=['table'])(SOURCE.read_text())
    doc=Document()
    sec=doc.sections[0]
    sec.page_width=Inches(8.5);sec.page_height=Inches(11)
    sec.top_margin=Inches(.73);sec.bottom_margin=Inches(.72)
    sec.left_margin=Inches(.82);sec.right_margin=Inches(.82)
    sec.header_distance=Inches(.30);sec.footer_distance=Inches(.38)
    styles=doc.styles
    normal=styles['Normal'];normal.font.name=FONT;normal.font.size=Pt(10.5);normal.font.color.rgb=DARK
    normal.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(7.0);normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing=1.16
    for kind,size,before,after,col in [('Title',21,0,12,DARK),('Heading 1',15.5,15,7,GREEN),('Heading 2',12.2,11,6,GREEN)]:
        s=styles[kind];s.font.name=FONT;s.font.size=Pt(size);s.font.bold=True;s.font.color.rgb=col
        s.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(before);s.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(after)
        s.paragraph_format.keep_with_next=True
    bp=styles['List Bullet'];bp.font.name=FONT;bp.font.size=Pt(10.3)
    bp.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(3)
    footer=sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    footer.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    r=footer.add_run('GMRI  /  GENERATIVE REASONING  /  V3.0     ');r.font.size=Pt(8);r.font.color.rgb=GRAY
    page_field(footer)
    first=True
    for node in ast:
        tp=node['type']
        if tp=='heading':
            level=node['attrs']['level']
            p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Title' if level==1 and first else 'Heading 1' if level==2 else 'Heading 2')
            add_inlines(p,node['children'])
            first=False
        elif tp=='paragraph':
            p=doc.add_paragraph()
            add_inlines(p,node['children'])
        elif tp=='list':
            for item in node['children']:
                p=doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet')
                body=item['children'][0]
                add_inlines(p,body.get('children',[]))
        elif tp=='table':
            head=node['children'][0]['children']; body=node['children'][1]['children']
            columns=len(head)
            table=doc.add_table(rows=1,cols=columns)
            table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
            table.style='Table Grid'
            table.autofit=False
            widths=([Inches(2.0),Inches(2.85),Inches(2.0)] if columns==3 else [Inches(3.43)]*columns)
            for j,c in enumerate(head):
                cell=table.rows[0].cells[j];cell.width=widths[j]
                cell.text=txt(c)
                shade(cell,'DFEAE1');cell_padding(cell)
                cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
                for para in cell.paragraphs:
                    para.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
                    for run in para.runs:run.bold=True;run.font.name=FONT;run.font.size=Pt(8.9);run.font.color.rgb=GREEN
            set_repeat(table.rows[0]);cant_split(table.rows[0])
            for row in body:
                cells=table.add_row().cells
                for j,element in enumerate(row['children']):
                    cell=cells[j];cell.width=widths[j];cell.text=txt(element)
                    cell.vertical_alignment=WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
                    cell_padding(cell,top=98,bottom=98,left=105,right=105)
                    for p in cell.paragraphs:
                        p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
                        p.paragraph_format.line_spacing=1.08
                        for run in p.runs:
                            run.font.name=FONT;run.font.size=Pt(9.0);run.font.color.rgb=DARK
                cant_split(table.rows[-1])
            after=doc.add_paragraph();after.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
        elif tp=='block_code':
            p=doc.add_paragraph()
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(.16)
            p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(10)
            p.paragraph_format.keep_together=True
            for line in node.get('raw','').strip('\n').splitlines():
                r=p.add_run(line+'\n');r.font.name='Consolas';r.font.size=Pt(8.15);r.font.color.rgb=GREEN
            pp=p._p.get_or_add_pPr();shade_node=OxmlElement('w:shd');shade_node.set(qn('w:fill'),'EFF5F0');pp.append(shade_node)
        elif tp=='blank_line':continue
        else:
            p=doc.add_paragraph(txt(node))
    doc.save(OUT)
    print(str(OUT))

if __name__=='__main__':build()
